skills.name: third-party-access-review

skills.description: Review third-party access into your environment — vendor and contractor accounts, MSP/RMM tools, remote support sessions, B2B guest users, partner VPNs, API integrations, OAuth apps and cloud cross-account roles — for necessity, least privilege, MFA, monitoring and expiry. Use for periodic vendor access reviews, MSP security assessments, or after a supply-chain incident.

skills.name: vendor-incident-response
skills.title: Vendor Incident Response
skills.description: Respond when a vendor, SaaS provider, MSP or software supplier is breached — determine exposure of your data and access, contain integrations (tokens, VPN, accounts, API keys), hunt for downstream compromise, manage contractual and regulatory notifications, and track vendor remediation. Use when a supplier announces or is reported to have a security incident affecting customers.

skills.name: vendor-security-assessment
skills.title: Vendor Security Assessment
skills.description: Assess third-party and SaaS vendor security proportionate to risk — tiering by data and access, evidence-based review (SOC 2, ISO certificates, pen test summaries, SIG/CAIQ questionnaires), external posture signals, contract security clauses, and continuous monitoring. Use when onboarding a vendor, renewing a contract, or building a third-party risk management program.

skills.name: beaconing-hunt
skills.title: Beaconing Hunt
skills.description: Hunt for command-and-control beaconing in proxy, firewall, Zeek or DNS logs using connection-interval regularity (jitter/coefficient of variation), data-size consistency, rarity and long-duration connections — includes a tested stdlib scoring script. Use when hunting for C2 without known IOCs, or validating a suspected implant's network pattern.

skills.name: hunt-data-readiness
skills.title: Hunt Data Readiness
skills.description: Verify that the telemetry needed for a hunt or detection actually exists, is complete and parsed correctly — source coverage by asset population, field population rates, retention, latency, clock skew and audit-policy settings. Use when preparing a hunt, before trusting a "no results" outcome, or when a detection silently never fires.

skills.name: hunt-to-detection
skills.title: Hunt to Detection
skills.description: Convert hunt findings into durable, tested detections — decide alert vs. dashboard vs. scheduled hunt, generalize from IOCs to behaviour, estimate volume, write Sigma/SIEM rules, and hand off with documentation. Use at the end of a hunt, or when a manual query keeps being re-run and should become automated.

skills.name: hypothesis-hunt
skills.title: Hypothesis-Driven Hunt
skills.description: Plan and execute a hypothesis-driven threat hunt (PEAK / TaHiTI style) — form a testable hypothesis from intel or ATT&CK, confirm data readiness, query, analyze, and document results including negative findings and new detections. Use when starting a proactive hunt, turning a threat report into hunting activity, or structuring a hunting program.

skills.name: lolbin-hunt
skills.title: LOLBin Hunt
skills.description: Hunt for abuse of living-off-the-land binaries and scripts (LOLBAS/GTFOBins) — certutil, mshta, rundll32, regsvr32, bitsadmin, msbuild, wmic, installutil, curl, and Linux equivalents — using command-line patterns, parentage and network activity. Use when hunting fileless or signed-binary proxy execution, or when an alert involves a Microsoft-signed binary doing something unusual.

skills.name: stack-counting-hunt
skills.title: Stack Counting (Long-Tail) Hunt
skills.description: Hunt by stacking (frequency analysis / long-tail analysis) — count process paths, parent-child pairs, autoruns, services, user agents, DNS domains or scheduled tasks across the fleet to surface rare outliers. Use when looking for unknown malware or persistence without specific IOCs, or establishing baselines.

skills.name: campaign-correlation
skills.title: Campaign Correlation
skills.description: Correlate incidents and indicators into campaigns and activity clusters using the Diamond Model, infrastructure pivoting (passive DNS, certificates, WHOIS/RDAP, hosting patterns, JA3/JA4/JARM), malware code overlap and TTP similarity, with disciplined confidence and attribution caution. Use when linking multiple incidents, expanding infrastructure from one IOC, or assessing whether activity matches a known actor.

skills.name: intel-report-writing
skills.title: Intelligence Report Writing
skills.description: Write and review threat intelligence products — strategic, operational and tactical reports — with key judgments, estimative language (ICD 203 style), source reliability, ATT&CK-mapped TTPs, IOCs, and actionable recommendations tied to intelligence requirements. Use when producing intel briefs, threat assessments or advisories, or critically reviewing a vendor threat report.

skills.name: intel-to-detection
skills.title: Intel to Detection
skills.description: Turn threat intelligence (reports, advisories, IOC feeds) into defensive action — exposure check, retro-hunt, behaviour detections from TTPs, IOC watchlists with expiry, and mitigations — and track what was done. Use when a new threat report or CISA/vendor advisory arrives and you must answer "are we affected and are we covered?".

skills.name: intelligence-requirements
skills.title: Intelligence Requirements
skills.description: Define and maintain priority intelligence requirements (PIRs) and a threat profile — relevant actors, motivations, targeted technologies, crown jewels — and drive collection, production and feedback in the intelligence cycle. Use when starting or refocusing a CTI program, prioritizing feeds/vendors, or justifying what intel the SOC should act on.

skills.name: ioc-assessment
skills.title: IOC Assessment
skills.description: Extract, validate, enrich and score indicators of compromise (IPs, domains, URLs, hashes, emails) from reports, alerts or emails — with a bundled tested extractor that refangs/defangs and filters private IPs — then decide block, alert, hunt or discard with expiry. Use when receiving IOC lists from intel feeds, vendors, ISACs or incidents, or before loading indicators into blocking controls.

skills.name: stix-taxii-misp
skills.title: STIX/TAXII and MISP
skills.description: Exchange and manage threat intelligence with STIX 2.1, TAXII 2.1 and MISP — object modelling (indicator, malware, threat-actor, relationship, sighting), patterns, TLP markings, feed ingestion, PyMISP automation, warning lists and de-duplication. Use when consuming or publishing intel feeds, configuring a TIP, or converting reports into structured intelligence.

skills.name: emergency-vulnerability-response
skills.title: Emergency Vulnerability Response
skills.description: Run an emergency response to a critical, actively exploited vulnerability (zero-day or new KEV entry, e.g. on edge devices, file-transfer appliances or widely used libraries) — rapid exposure inventory, vendor mitigations, compromise assessment, patch tracking and communications. Use when a vendor/CISA emergency advisory drops or exploitation of a product you run is reported.

skills.name: exposure-validation
skills.title: Exposure Validation
skills.description: Safely validate whether a vulnerability is actually exposed and exploitable in your environment — reachability, version confirmation, configuration preconditions, non-destructive checks (nmap NSE safe scripts, nuclei with vetted templates, vendor detection scripts) — without causing outages. Use when deciding whether a reported vulnerability is real for a given asset, or confirming remediation.

skills.name: patch-campaign
skills.title: Patch Campaign
skills.description: Plan and run a patch or remediation campaign — scoping affected assets, rollout rings, maintenance windows, rollback, owner communication, progress tracking and verification — for OS, application, firmware or cloud image updates. Use when a vulnerability or set of fixes must be deployed across many systems on a deadline.

skills.name: scan-result-triage
skills.title: Scan Result Triage
skills.description: Triage vulnerability scanner output (Tenable/Nessus, Qualys, Rapid7, OpenVAS, Trivy, cloud-native scanners) — deduplicate, validate detection method (authenticated vs. banner), identify false positives and backported patches, group by fix, and measure scan coverage. Use when a new scan report arrives, findings are disputed by system owners, or scan coverage is in question.

skills.name: vuln-exception-review
skills.title: Vulnerability Exception Review
skills.description: Review vulnerability risk-acceptance and exception requests — justification, compensating controls, residual risk, approver authority, expiry and re-review — and audit the existing exception register for stale or unjustified entries. Use when a team asks to defer or accept a vulnerability, or during periodic exception audits.

skills.name: vuln-prioritization
skills.title: Vulnerability Prioritization
skills.description: Prioritize vulnerabilities by real risk using CISA KEV, EPSS, CVSS v4/v3.1, SSVC decision trees, asset criticality and exposure, rather than CVSS score alone, and set remediation SLAs. Use when a scan produces too many findings, when building a patch priority list, or when someone asks "which of these CVEs matter?".

skills.name: credential-stuffing-defense
skills.title: Credential Stuffing Defense
skills.description: Detect and mitigate credential stuffing and account takeover against customer-facing login, registration and password-reset endpoints — traffic signals (distributed IPs, residential proxies, high failure rates, user-agent patterns), bot management, rate limiting, breached-password checks, MFA/passkeys, and response for compromised customer accounts. Use when login failures spike, customers report account takeovers, or designing consumer authentication defenses.

skills.name: waf-rule-tuning
skills.title: WAF Rule Tuning
skills.description: Tune web application firewalls (OWASP Core Rule Set on ModSecurity/Coraza, AWS WAF, Azure WAF, Cloudflare, Akamai) — paranoia levels and anomaly thresholds, false-positive exclusions scoped by rule, path and parameter, detect-to-block rollout, virtual patching for new CVEs, and log review. Use when deploying a WAF, when it blocks legitimate traffic, or when a virtual patch is needed before an application fix.

skills.name: web-server-log-analysis
skills.title: Web Server Log Analysis
skills.description: Analyze web server, reverse proxy, load balancer and WAF logs (Apache, Nginx, IIS, ALB, CloudFront, Azure Front Door) for exploitation attempts and successes — injection, path traversal, web shell access, scanning, credential attacks — distinguishing noise from successful compromise. Use when investigating a possible web application breach, triaging WAF alerts, or hunting web attacks.

skills.name: web-shell-detection
skills.title: Web Shell Detection
skills.description: Detect and remove web shells on IIS, Apache, Nginx/PHP-FPM, Tomcat and Exchange/SharePoint servers — file-based indicators (new script files in web roots, obfuscation), process indicators (web server spawning shells), network/log indicators — with YARA, file integrity baselines and EDR queries. Use after web application exploitation, when hunting on internet-facing servers, or following edge-application vulnerability advisories.

skills.name: credential-theft-detection
skills.title: Credential Theft Detection (Windows)
skills.description: Detect and investigate Windows credential theft — LSASS memory access and dumping (Mimikatz, comsvcs MiniDump, procdump), SAM/SECURITY/NTDS.dit extraction, DPAPI and browser credential theft — and harden against it (Credential Guard, RunAsPPL). Use when an alert mentions LSASS, credential dumping, or after confirmed hands-on-keyboard activity.

skills.name: lateral-movement-detection
skills.title: Lateral Movement Detection
skills.description: Detect and trace Windows lateral movement — PsExec/service creation, WMI, WinRM/PowerShell remoting, RDP, SMB admin shares, DCOM, scheduled tasks and pass-the-hash/ticket — by correlating source and destination host events. Use when an attacker may be moving between hosts or when mapping the path of a compromise.

skills.name: powershell-logging
skills.title: PowerShell Logging and Analysis
skills.description: Enable and analyze PowerShell telemetry — script block logging (4104), module logging (4103), transcription, AMSI — to detect encoded commands, download cradles, obfuscation and downgrade attacks. Use when investigating malicious PowerShell, reviewing logging configuration, or writing PowerShell detections.

skills.name: sysmon-deployment
skills.title: Sysmon Deployment and Tuning
skills.description: Deploy, tune and validate Microsoft Sysmon — configuration selection (sysmon-modular, SwiftOnSecurity), event coverage, noise reduction, update and health monitoring. Use when planning Windows endpoint telemetry, reviewing a Sysmon config, or troubleshooting missing Sysmon events.

skills.name: windows-event-log-analysis
skills.title: Windows Event Log Analysis
skills.description: Investigate Windows Security, System, PowerShell, Sysmon, RDP, Task Scheduler and Defender event logs — logons, process creation, service/task installs, account changes, log clearing — with Get-WinEvent, Hayabusa, Chainsaw or SIEM queries. Use when analysing EVTX files or Windows events in a SIEM during triage, hunting or forensics.

skills.name: windows-persistence-hunt
skills.title: Windows Persistence Hunt
skills.description: Hunt for and validate Windows persistence — Run keys, services, scheduled tasks, WMI event subscriptions, startup folders, IFEO, COM hijacks, LSA/Winlogon, BITS jobs — using Autoruns, PowerShell, EDR and event logs. Use when sweeping hosts after a compromise, hunting for footholds, or verifying eradication.

skills.name: enterprise-wifi-review
skills.title: Enterprise Wi-Fi Review
skills.description: Review enterprise Wi-Fi security — WPA3-Enterprise/WPA2-Enterprise with 802.1X, EAP method choice (EAP-TLS vs. PEAP-MSCHAPv2), supplicant server-certificate validation, PSK networks, guest isolation, management frame protection, segmentation of SSIDs to VLANs, and NAC posture. Use when assessing wireless networks, migrating to certificate-based Wi-Fi, or after evil-twin/credential capture concerns.

skills.name: radius-log-investigation
skills.title: RADIUS Log Investigation
skills.description: Investigate network access authentication using RADIUS/NPS/ISE/ClearPass/FreeRADIUS logs — 802.1X Wi-Fi and wired access, VPN authentication, failure reasons, MAC authentication bypass abuse, accounting records (session start/stop, IP, bytes) — to attribute devices and users to network sessions. Use when tracing who was on the network at a time, investigating authentication failures or spoofed MAB devices, or correlating network sessions with incidents.

skills.name: rogue-ap-detection
skills.title: Rogue AP Detection
skills.description: Detect and handle rogue and evil-twin access points, unauthorized wireless bridges and hotspots using WLAN controller/WIPS data, wired-side correlation (switch MAC tables, NAC), and authorized RF surveys with Kismet — and decide on containment lawfully. Use when WIPS reports rogue APs, users report suspicious SSIDs, or performing periodic wireless audits (e.g., PCI DSS 11.2).
